title: Big questions call for big telescopes
caption: A Unit Telescope of the Very Large Telescope under a clear night sky, Paranal Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: One of the four Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope stands under a clear night sky at Paranal Observatory, in a photograph by Daniele Gasparri.

Each Unit Telescope has a main mirror 8.2 meters across, which puts them among the largest single-mirror telescopes in the world. A bigger mirror collects more light, and that lets astronomers study fainter and more distant objects.

The four can observe separately or together. When their light is combined they are equivalent to a single-mirror telescope 16 meters across, effectively the largest optical telescope in the world, according to ESO. The work done here feeds a steady flow of research. On average the Very Large Telescope leads to more than one peer-reviewed scientific paper a day, as astronomers use it to tackle some of the biggest questions about the Universe.

understand.summary: A ground-based photograph by Daniele Gasparri for ESO, taken in visible light. The colors are those the camera recorded.
understand.eye: A camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the night sky probably shows more stars in the photograph than a visitor would see.
